public_rationale: The narrower warning about insecure output has substantial support. Research documents serious vulnerabilities in deployed applications and agents shipping code despite recognizing security risks. The broader contextual claim—that this practice is contributing to rising cybersecurity and infrastructure failures—remains unestablished by these records. Vulnerability findings alone do not demonstrate exploitation or explain a trend in failures.
limitations: A general security-risk reading would be better supported than the broader causal reading assessed here.
The deployed-application study covers selected tools and public repositories.
The benchmark deliberately concentrates on security-sensitive tasks.

our_interpretation: Read recipe for disaster as a serious causal risk, not a prediction that every application must fail.
Read vibe coding as delegating substantial coding decisions to AI without competent review.
In context, the claim extends beyond the existence of vulnerabilities: it identifies this practice as contributing to rising cybersecurity and infrastructure failures.
Do not require attribution of every outage mentioned in the post, but require evidence connecting the coding practice to serious failures rather than merely showing insecure output.
criteria.support_condition: Comparative security research and incident investigations establish that insufficiently reviewed AI-generated code materially increases exploitable vulnerabilities and contributes to serious cybersecurity or infrastructure failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Strong comparative evidence and relevant incident investigations establish that the claimed increase in security risk and contribution to failures does not hold.

evidence.locator: Section 7, discussion of the awareness–action gap
evidence.publisher: Junquan Deng, Zhiyu Fan and Ruijie Meng / arXiv
evidence.explanation: The study reports vulnerabilities in 91% of 200 audited deployed applications and investigates recurring agent failure mechanisms. It supports the security-risk component, but does not establish that this workflow caused the rise in infrastructure failures described by Marcus.

evidence.publisher: Songwen Zhao and colleagues / ICML 2026, arXiv version
evidence.explanation: The benchmark finds a large gap between functional and secure solutions. Its tasks were selected from cases where human programmers also produced vulnerable implementations, so it does not by itself establish a general causal disadvantage or realized infrastructure damage.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Incident investigations tracing substantial failures to insufficiently reviewed AI-generated code, together with comparative evidence separating this effect from developer skill and other workflow differences.
